analysis.title: U.S. Equities Intraday Color
key_insights: S&P 500 is sharply higher on 4 Nov 2026 after the midterm election. The desk says investors are surprised by the size of the reversal.

Since 1952 the 12 months after a midterm election have been the strongest stretch of the four-year cycle for the S&P 500. Across 18 midterms the index averaged +7.5% through year end, +13.9% over the next 6 months and +15.5% over 12 months. It was higher at both the 6-month and 12-month marks in all 18 cases.

Two drivers of the rally are named: President Trump told the NYT he would accept the election results, which removed some left-tail risk, and crude is down 8%, which traders link to a possible faster end to the Iran conflict under a Blue Wave.

The standout theme on the GS trading desk is buying hyperscalers versus selling semiconductors. The reasoning is that if compute capacity cannot be expanded, compute is scarcer and sells at a higher price, spending falls, and freed cash could go to share buybacks.
Equity investors across all cohorts have had a difficult stretch since July. Significant risk has been cut, hedge fund net exposure is historically low, and gross exposure ticked lower last week.
Long-only funds hold a significant amount of cash raised during the July and October selloffs. Most of it has not been redeployed because trading has stayed choppy.

October is the largest month for mutual fund fiscal year ends by both AUM and number of funds. Long-only managers sold stocks on Friday 10/30 because of year-end dynamics, which set up the midterms as a clean clearing event for positioning.
The desk says the most important potential clearing event this year is still ahead and is tied to equity capital markets.

sector_views.rationale: The desk is buying hyperscalers because scarce compute capacity supports pricing, lowers capex needs and frees cash for buybacks.
The desk is selling semis against the hyperscaler buying, though the note gives no separate reasoning for the semis side.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Crude fell 8% on the day. The desk says this helps stocks because traders hope a Blue Wave could bring an earlier end to the Iran conflict.
